description: Comprehensive UX Assessment Guidelines - Including Usability, Accessibility, and UX Heuristics Standards

usability.name: Usability
usability.description: Jakob Nielsen's foundational principles for interaction design

principles.name: Visibility of system status
principles.description: The design should always keep users informed about what is going on, through appropriate feedback within a reasonable amount of time

examples.good: Clear loading spinner with percentage, success toast notifications
examples.bad: No feedback when action is processing, silent failures

principles.name: Match between system and real world
principles.description: The design should speak the users' language. Use words, phrases, and concepts familiar to the user, rather than internal jargon

principles.name: User control and freedom
principles.description: Users need a clearly marked 'emergency exit' to leave an unwanted action without having to go through an extended process

principles.name: Consistency and standards
principles.description: Users should not have to wonder whether different words, situations, or actions mean the same thing

principles.name: Error prevention
principles.description: Good error messages are important, but the best designs carefully prevent problems from occurring in the first place

principles.name: Recognition rather than recall
principles.description: Minimize the user's memory load by making elements, actions, and options visible

principles.name: Flexibility and efficiency of use
principles.description: Shortcuts — hidden from novice users — may speed up the interaction for the expert user

principles.name: Aesthetic and minimalist design
principles.description: Interfaces should not contain information that is irrelevant or rarely needed

principles.name: Help users recognize, diagnose, and recover from errors
principles.description: Error messages should be expressed in plain language, precisely indicate the problem, and constructively suggest a solution

principles.name: Help and documentation
principles.description: It's best if the system doesn't need any additional explanation. However, it may be necessary to provide documentation

accessibility.name: Accessibility
accessibility.description: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines - ensuring inclusive design for all users

principles.name: Perceivable
principles.description: Information and user interface components must be presentable to users in ways they can perceive

guidelines.name: Text Alternatives
guidelines.description: Provide text alternatives for non-text content

guidelines.name: Adaptable
guidelines.description: Create content that can be presented in different ways without losing information

guidelines.name: Distinguishable
guidelines.description: Make it easier for users to see and hear content

principles.name: Operable
principles.description: User interface components and navigation must be operable

guidelines.name: Keyboard Accessible
guidelines.description: Make all functionality available from a keyboard

guidelines.name: Enough Time
guidelines.description: Provide users enough time to read and use content
checkpoints: Pause, stop, hide for moving content

guidelines.name: Seizures and Physical Reactions
guidelines.description: Do not design content in a way that is known to cause seizures
checkpoints: No content flashes more than 3 times per second
Animation from interactions can be disabled

guidelines.name: Navigable
guidelines.description: Provide ways to help users navigate and find content

guidelines.name: Input Modalities
guidelines.description: Make it easier for users to operate functionality through various inputs
checkpoints: Pointer gestures can be operated with single pointer
Label in name matches accessible name

principles.name: Understandable
principles.description: Information and the operation of user interface must be understandable

guidelines.name: Readable
guidelines.description: Make text content readable and understandable

guidelines.name: Predictable
guidelines.description: Make web pages appear and operate in predictable ways
checkpoints: On focus doesn't trigger unexpected changes
On input doesn't trigger unexpected changes

guidelines.name: Input Assistance
guidelines.description: Help users avoid and correct mistakes

principles.name: Robust
principles.description: Content must be robust enough that it can be interpreted by a wide variety of user agents, including assistive technologies

guidelines.name: Compatible
guidelines.description: Maximize compatibility with current and future user agents
checkpoints: Name, role, value available for all UI components

visual.name: Visual Design
visual.description: Core principles for effective visual communication and aesthetic appeal

principles.name: Hierarchy
principles.description: Organize and prioritize content to guide users through the interface

principles.name: Balance
principles.description: Distribute visual weight to create stability and structure

principles.name: Contrast
principles.description: Create visual interest and draw attention to important elements

principles.name: Repetition
principles.description: Create consistency and strengthen overall design unity

principles.name: Proximity
principles.description: Group related items together to show relationships

principles.name: Alignment
principles.description: Create visual connections and organize information

principles.name: White Space
principles.description: Use negative space to improve readability and focus

principles.name: Color
principles.description: Use color purposefully to communicate and evoke emotion

principles.name: Typography
principles.description: Choose and implement type to enhance readability and brand

principles.name: Imagery
principles.description: Use images purposefully to support content and messaging

principles.name: Grid Systems
principles.description: Use structural frameworks to organize content consistently

principles.name: Consistency
principles.description: Maintain uniform design language throughout the experience

scoringGuidelines.description: Guidelines for scoring designs across evaluation dimensions

excellent.description: Exemplary design that exceeds industry standards
characteristics: All accessibility requirements met or exceeded
Polished visual design with strong hierarchy

good.description: Solid design with minor areas for improvement
characteristics: Good visual design with clear hierarchy

fair.description: Acceptable design with notable issues to address

poor.description: Significant issues that impact user experience

high.description: Blocks core functionality or creates significant barriers
examples: Critical information unreadable due to contrast

low.description: Minor polish issues that don't significantly impact usability

usability.rationale: Core user experience and task completion effectiveness

accessibility.rationale: Inclusive design ensuring usability for all users

mobile.name: Mobile-Specific Considerations
mobile.description: Special considerations for mobile interfaces and touch interactions
checkpoints: Thumb-friendly primary actions in bottom third of screen
Network performance consideration for slow connections

desktop.name: Desktop-Specific Considerations
desktop.description: Optimizations for desktop and large screen experiences
checkpoints: Keyboard shortcuts available for common actions
Effective hover states for interactive elements
Large screen utilization (not just centered narrow content)

tablet.name: Tablet-Specific Considerations
checkpoints: Touch targets appropriate for finger interaction
Layout optimized for medium screen sizes
Support for both portrait and landscape

flow.name: User Flow Considerations
flow.description: Evaluating multi-step processes and task flows
checkpoints: Clear progress indication throughout the flow
Easy backward navigation without data loss
Save and resume capability for long flows
commonIssues: Loss of data when navigating backward
No clear completion or next steps

forms.name: Form Design Considerations
forms.description: Best practices for form design and input collection
checkpoints: Clear labels for all input fields
Input validation with clear error messages
Appropriate input types for data (email, tel, etc.)
Clear required vs. optional field indication

dataVisualization.name: Data Visualization Considerations
dataVisualization.description: Guidelines for charts, graphs, and data displays
checkpoints: Accessible color schemes (not relying solely on color)
Appropriate chart types for data being shown
Consistent formatting of numbers and dates

accessibility.impact: Users with low vision or color blindness cannot read content
accessibility.solution: Ensure minimum 4.5:1 contrast ratio for normal text, 3:1 for large text (18pt+ or 14pt+ bold)
accessibility.howToTest: Use browser DevTools or online contrast checkers

accessibility.impact: Screen reader users cannot understand image content
accessibility.solution: Add descriptive alt text for all informative images, use alt='' for decorative images
accessibility.howToTest: Check HTML for alt attributes, test with screen reader

accessibility.impact: Difficult to tap accurately, especially for users with motor impairments
accessibility.solution: Increase interactive element size to at least 44x44px with adequate spacing
accessibility.howToTest: Measure button and link sizes in browser DevTools

accessibility.impact: Keyboard users cannot track their position in the interface
accessibility.solution: Add clear focus indicators with adequate contrast (3:1 minimum)
accessibility.howToTest: Navigate interface using Tab key and observe focus visibility

accessibility.impact: Screen reader users and users with cognitive disabilities cannot identify field purpose
accessibility.solution: Provide visible labels or properly associated ARIA labels for all inputs
accessibility.howToTest: Test with screen reader, check for label elements or aria-label

accessibility.impact: Screen reader users cannot efficiently navigate page content
accessibility.solution: Use proper heading hierarchy (h1-h6) to structure content logically
accessibility.howToTest: Check HTML structure or use heading outline tools

accessibility.impact: Distracts users and interferes with screen readers
accessibility.solution: Provide pause/stop controls or limit auto-play to 5 seconds
accessibility.howToTest: Load page and observe any auto-playing content

usability.impact: Users struggle to identify and complete primary task
usability.solution: Increase visual weight of primary CTA through size, color, or position
usability.howToTest: Show to users and ask what the primary action is

usability.impact: Users don't know if actions are processing or completed
usability.solution: Add loading indicators, progress bars, and success/error messages
usability.howToTest: Perform actions and observe feedback provided

usability.impact: Users can accidentally perform destructive actions
usability.solution: Add confirmation dialogs for destructive actions, disable submit until valid
usability.howToTest: Try to delete or modify data and check for confirmation

usability.impact: Users must relearn navigation in different sections
usability.solution: Standardize navigation patterns across all screens
usability.howToTest: Navigate through different sections and compare patterns

usability.impact: Users cannot understand or fix errors
usability.solution: Provide clear, specific error messages with actionable recovery steps
usability.howToTest: Trigger errors and evaluate message clarity

usability.impact: Users get lost or cannot find features
usability.solution: Make navigation visible and clearly labeled
usability.howToTest: Ask users to find specific features

visual.impact: Users cannot quickly scan and understand content importance
visual.solution: Use size, color, weight, and spacing to establish clear importance levels
visual.howToTest: Blur the design and see if structure is still apparent

visual.impact: Content feels cramped and difficult to parse
visual.solution: Increase spacing between elements, especially around important content
visual.howToTest: Check spacing consistency and breathing room

visual.solution: Create and apply a unified design system with consistent patterns
visual.howToTest: Compare similar components across different screens

visual.solution: Use appropriate font sizes (16px+ for body), line height (1.5+), and line length
visual.howToTest: Read extended content and evaluate comfort

visual.impact: Cognitive overload and difficulty finding information
visual.solution: Group related elements, remove unnecessary content, use progressive disclosure
visual.howToTest: Count distinct visual elements and information groups

evaluationProcess.description: Systematic process for conducting UX assessments

steps.name: Context Analysis
steps.description: Understand the design context and constraints
activities: Determine use case (user flow, single screen, feature)
Note any specific constraints or requirements

steps.name: Systematic Evaluation
activities: Assess accessibility using WCAG POUR principles

steps.name: Issue Identification
activities: Provide specific examples from the design
Link to relevant standards or guidelines

steps.name: Recommendation Development
activities: Suggest specific solutions for each issue

steps.name: Scoring
activities: Deduct points based on issue severity

modifiers.multipleHighIssues: Apply diminishing returns for similar issues
modifiers.positiveElements: Note strengths but focus on improvement areas
modifiers.context: Consider device type and use case when scoring

content: Strengths to maintain and build upon

communicationPrinciples.constructive: Focus on improvement opportunities, not just criticism
communicationPrinciples.specific: Provide concrete examples rather than vague observations
communicationPrinciples.actionable: Always suggest how to address identified issues
communicationPrinciples.balanced: Acknowledge both strengths and areas for improvement
communicationPrinciples.prioritized: Help readers focus on most impactful changes first
